# Infusion Device with Elastically Supported Sensor Configuration

The infusion device is constructed around a two-part housing arrangement designed to securely receive and retain a section of tubing from a tube set. The first housing element is configured to receive the tube section, while a movable second housing element functions as a closure. When brought into its closed position, this second element holds the tube section securely between the two housing components, ensuring that the tubing is properly seated and stabilized during operation.

To monitor the conditions within the tube set during use, a sensor device is mounted on the first housing element. This sensor device incorporates a sensor element that measures the force acting on the tube section, thereby enabling the detection of pressure changes within the fluid path. Such measurements are essential for reliable infusion performance and for identifying potential occlusions or other irregularities in the flow.

A key feature of this configuration is the manner in which the sensor device is mounted. Rather than being fixed rigidly in place, the sensor device is arranged on the first housing element so as to be elastically displaceable. This is achieved through support provided by at least one spring element, which allows the sensor device a limited degree of movement in response to applied forces.

This elastic support design offers a significant functional advantage. Because the sensor device can accommodate slight variations in position, the overall device becomes less susceptible to inconsistencies in the way the tube section is squeezed between the sensor element and the movable housing element. Variations in tube compression—which might otherwise distort measurement results—are effectively buffered by the spring-supported arrangement.

As a result of this configuration, the infusion device offers two notable benefits. First, it has the potential to reduce the calibration effort typically required for such devices, since the elastic support compensates for mechanical variations that would otherwise necessitate more extensive calibration procedures. Second, it increases the reliability of pressure measurements taken on the tube section, providing more consistent and dependable monitoring throughout the infusion process.

# Infusion Device with Spring-Supported Sensor Arrangement

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to an infusion device for the controlled transport of a medical fluid through a tube set. Such devices are commonly employed in clinical and outpatient settings to deliver medication, nutrition, or other therapeutic fluids to a patient at a precisely regulated flow rate. In particular, the invention concerns an improved arrangement for the reliable measurement of pressure or force conditions within the fluid line during operation.

## Background

Infusion devices, such as peristaltic or volumetric pumps, typically operate by receiving a section of flexible tubing and conveying fluid through it by means of a pumping mechanism. During operation, it is important to monitor the pressure within the tube in order to detect abnormal conditions such as occlusions, air-in-line, or empty containers. An excessive rise in pressure may indicate a downstream blockage, while a drop in pressure may signal an upstream disconnection or an exhausted fluid supply.

Conventional infusion devices often incorporate a sensor element that measures the force exerted by the tube section as fluid passes through it. However, the accuracy of such measurements can be compromised by manufacturing tolerances in the tubing, variations in wall thickness, and inconsistencies in the degree to which the tube is compressed, or "squeezed," between the sensor and the surrounding housing components. These variations can necessitate extensive calibration procedures and may reduce the overall reliability of the pressure readings.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention addresses these shortcomings by providing an infusion device with an improved sensor arrangement. The device comprises two housing elements that cooperatively receive a section of the tube set. A first housing element and a second, movable housing element are arranged such that the tube section is positioned between them. When the housing is closed, the tube is held in a defined position for measurement and fluid transport.

A sensor device is provided, incorporating a sensor element configured to measure the force acting upon it as a result of the pressure within the tube section. In accordance with the invention, the sensor device is not rigidly fixed in place. Instead, it is elastically displaceable and is supported on the first housing element by way of at least one spring element. This spring element permits the sensor device to yield resiliently in response to the force applied by the tube and the movable housing element.

## Advantages

The spring-supported design of the sensor device offers several significant advantages. Because the sensor device can displace elastically against the biasing force of the spring element, the degree to which the tube section is squeezed between the sensor element and the movable housing element remains substantially more consistent, even in the presence of dimensional tolerances in the tubing or in the components themselves. The elastic mounting effectively compensates for such variations, ensuring that the tube is compressed to a more uniform and predictable extent.

As a result, the variability in tube squeezing that has traditionally affected pressure measurements is reduced. This, in turn, lowers the calibration effort required to prepare the device for accurate operation, since fewer corrections are needed to account for tube-to-tube or unit-to-unit variation. Furthermore, the consistency afforded by the spring-supported arrangement improves the overall reliability and accuracy of the pressure measurements obtained during infusion.

## Conclusion

In summary, the described infusion device provides a robust and reliable means of transporting medical fluid while accurately monitoring line pressure. By supporting the sensor device on the first housing element via at least one spring element, the invention achieves a more consistent compression of the tube section, thereby reducing calibration requirements and enhancing measurement dependability. This contributes to safer and more effective delivery of medical fluids to the patient.

counterfactuals.output:
# Abstract

An infusion device for delivering fluid to a patient includes a housing configured to receive a tube set through which fluid flows. A force sensor is positioned adjacent to the tube set and configured to measure a force exerted by the tube set, the force being representative of fluid pressure within the tube set. The force sensor generates a signal corresponding to the measured force, which is transmitted to a controller. The controller processes the signal to determine a pressure value associated with fluid flow through the tube set and compares the determined pressure value to one or more threshold values. In response to the comparison, the controller may generate an alert, adjust a delivery parameter, or halt fluid delivery to mitigate conditions such as occlusion, air-in-line, or disconnection. The force sensor may include a load cell, strain gauge, or piezoelectric element positioned to contact a wall of the tube set when the tube set is loaded into the housing. In certain embodiments, the device includes a calibration mechanism to account for variations in tube set properties and mounting conditions, thereby improving measurement accuracy. The disclosed infusion device provides real-time monitoring of fluid pressure, enhancing patient safety and delivery precision during infusion therapy.

# ABSTRACT

An infusion pump device for administering medical fluids through a tubing section is disclosed. The device comprises a first housing element (10) and a second housing element (20) that are movably coupled to define a receiving region (30) for accommodating a medical tubing section (40). A sensor (50) is arranged within the first housing element (10) and is elastically supported by a resilient element (60) configured to bias the sensor (50) toward the receiving region (30). When the tubing section (40) is positioned within the receiving region (30), the sensor (50) contacts the tubing section (40) and measures a force exerted thereon, the force being representative of a fluid pressure within the tubing section (40). The elastic support provided by the resilient element (60) permits displacement of the sensor (50) relative to the first housing element (10) in response to variations in the force, thereby enabling accurate detection of occlusions, air bubbles, or pressure anomalies during operation. The second housing element (20) is displaceable between an open position, in which the tubing section (40) can be inserted into or removed from the receiving region (30), and a closed position, in which the tubing section (40) is retained against the sensor (50). A control unit (70) coupled to the sensor (50) receives a signal corresponding to the measured force and regulates operation of the infusion pump device based thereon.

# Medical Fluid Infusion Device with Force-Sensing Occlusion Detection

## ABSTRACT

A medical fluid infusion device (100) for controlled delivery of fluid through a flexible tube (10) and configured to detect occlusion conditions via direct force measurement. The device comprises a first stationary housing (12) defining a mounting structure and an internal reference surface (14), and a movable second housing (16) mechanically coupled to the first stationary housing (12) and configured for translational displacement relative thereto along a defined axis (18). The flexible tube (10) is received within a channel (20) formed between the first stationary housing (12) and the movable second housing (16), such that relative movement of the movable second housing (16) applies a squeezing force (F) to the flexible tube (10).

A spring-supported sensor assembly (22) is disposed between the movable second housing (16) and the reference surface (14), the sensor assembly (22) comprising a biasing spring element (24) and a force transducer (26) operatively aligned with the flexible tube (10). The biasing spring element (24) supports the force transducer (26) in resilient contact with an outer wall of the flexible tube (10), whereby the force transducer (26) generates an electrical signal (28) proportional to the squeezing force (F) exerted on the flexible tube (10).

A controller (30) is electrically coupled to the force transducer (26) and configured to receive the electrical signal (28) and to compare a measured force value against a predetermined threshold (32). Upon detecting a deviation indicative of a downstream or upstream occlusion, the controller (30) actuates an alarm module (34) and/or modifies operation of a pump mechanism (36) driving the fluid. The spring-supported sensor assembly (22) compensates for dimensional tolerances of the flexible tube (10) and maintains consistent sensor preload across a range of tube diameters, thereby improving the accuracy and sensitivity of occlusion detection while reducing false alarms.

# Patent Abstract

**Infusion Device with Elastically Mounted Pressure Sensor for Improved Measurement Reliability**

An infusion device is disclosed comprising a pressure sensor for monitoring fluid pressure within a flexible infusion tube. The sensor is mounted in an elastically displaceable manner by means of a spring element, permitting controlled movement of the sensor relative to the tube-receiving portion of the device.

In conventional infusion devices, the infusion tube is positioned between a fixed sensor and an opposing surface, whereby dimensional tolerances in tube wall thickness, tube diameter, and mounting geometry produce inconsistent squeezing of the tube. Such variation in mechanical compression introduces error into the measured pressure signal, reducing the reliability of occlusion detection and pressure monitoring.

The present invention addresses this problem by resiliently biasing the sensor against the tube via the spring. As the sensor is elastically displaceable, it accommodates variations in tube dimensions and positioning by adjusting its position under a substantially constant spring force. This arrangement maintains a consistent contact pressure and a reproducible degree of tube deformation across differing tubes and mounting conditions.

By reducing variation in tube squeezing, the elastic mounting establishes a more uniform mechanical coupling between the tube and the sensor, thereby yielding a more accurate and repeatable relationship between the measured signal and the actual fluid pressure. The device consequently provides improved pressure measurement reliability, enhanced occlusion detection, and reduced susceptibility to component tolerances during operation.
